title: Mrs. Mina Mikhlia Velichansky

page_data.en:
CONFIDENTIAL
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
No. S. B. D. 8979
Section 1, Special Branch
REPORT
Date February 4, 1939
Subject Communication dated 23-1-39 from the Italian Consulate-General
concerning Mrs. M.M. Velichansky.
Made by D.S.I. Prokofiev. Forwarded by C. Gauson
Enquiries show that Mina Mikhlia VELICHANSKY, age
about 25, Russian of Jewish origin, arrived in Shanghai from
Manchuria in 1931 together with her mother, Mrs. S.S. Velichan-
sky, 47, a widow. The latter conducted a licensed boarding
house at 23 Chusan Road from 1932 to June, 1937 and is now re-
siding at 7 Route de Grouchy, Apt. 10.
Miss Velichansky is known to have been employed as
a shop assistant with Whiteaway, Laidlaw & Co., Ltd., 98 Nanking
Road, from 1932 to 1934, during which period she resided with
her mother. Early in 1934 she married one Mr. A. Meyer, a
French citizen of Jewish extraction, who for many years has
been in the employ of Sennet Freres, Jewellers, 307 Hamilton
House. Following their marriage Mr. and Mrs Meyer went to live
at 209 Embankment Building.
It appears that some time in 1937 they separated,
after which Mrs Velichansky-Meyer resided with her mother un-
til 14-7-38 when she left for Singapore in the s.s. "Conte
Verde". When booking her passage she was in possession of a
passport or some other document of identity issued by the lo-
cal French Consulate-General. She is believed to be employed
with a firm in Singapore, her present address in that city being
given as 8 Institution Hill (?).
Neither Mrs Velichansky nor any member of her fa-
mily are known at the Russian Emigrants' Committee, 118/1 Moul-
mein Road, or at the Council of United Russian Organization
(SORO), 8 Avenue Dubail, with one of which public bodies local
Russian emigrants are usually registered. However, Mrs S.S.
Velichansky registered with the French Police in 1938 as a Rus-
sian emigrant. There are reasons to believe that the Velichan-

日期：1939年2月4日
事由：意大利总领事馆1939年1月23日来函，涉及M.M. Velichansky夫人。
由特别调查员普罗科菲耶夫（Prokofiev）呈报。由高森（C. Gauson）转呈
经查，米娜·米赫利亚·韦利昌斯基（Mina Mikhlia VELICHANSKY），年龄约25岁，犹太裔俄国人，于1931年与其母亲S.S. 韦利昌斯基夫人（47岁，寡妇）一同从满洲抵达上海。后者自1932年至1937年6月在中山路23号经营一家持牌寄宿舍，现居住于格鲁希路（Route de Grouchy）7号10室。
据悉，韦利昌斯基小姐于1932年至1934年间受雇于南京路98号的惠罗公司（Whiteaway, Laidlaw & Co., Ltd.）担任店员，在此期间她与母亲同住。1934年初，她嫁给一位名叫A. 迈耶（A. Meyer）的先生，此人为犹太裔法国公民，多年来受雇于汉密尔顿大楼307号的森内特兄弟珠宝行（Sennet Freres, Jewellers）。婚后，迈耶夫妇搬至外滩公寓209号居住。
看来他们在1937年的某个时候分居，此后韦利昌斯基-迈耶夫人与其母亲同住，直到1938年7月14日乘“绿伯爵”号轮船（s.s. "Conte Verde"）前往新加坡。在预订船票时，她持有由当地法国总领事馆签发的护照或其他身份证明文件。据信她在新加坡的一家公司任职，其在该市的现住址列为机构山（Institution Hill）8号（？）。
在慕尔鸣路118/1号的俄国侨民委员会，或在杜巴伊路8号的全俄组织联合会（SORO），均无人知晓韦利昌斯基夫人或其任何家庭成员；通常本地俄国侨民会在上述某一公共机构登记。然而，S.S. 韦利昌斯基夫人曾于1938年向法国警察登记为俄国侨民。有理由相信，韦利昌

sky family were originally Soviet citizens and that they re-
nounced their allegiance to the Soviet government upon arrival
in Shanghai and took out emigrant papers at the Shanghai City
Government Police Bureau, Nantao, as this Bureau ceased to
function following the occupation of Shanghai by the Japanese
troops, no official information is available regarding this

        While in Shanghai neither Mrs Velichansky-Meyer nor

Police in connection with any activities of an undesirable na-

        在上海期间，韦利昌斯基-迈耶夫人及其任何家庭成员均未因任何不良性质的活动而引起工部局警务处的注意。

Consolato Generale d'Italia
N. 142.
Pos. A. 53/I.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. C. REGISTRY
No. S. B. D. 8979
Date 25 / 1 / 39

Shanghai, January 23rd, 1939 (XVII)

CONFIDENTIAL

Sir,

I should be grateful if you would kindly let
me have all possible information concerning Mrs. Mina
Mikhlia Velickansky, a Russian emigrant, born in Chita
(Siberia) on September 24th, 1914, holding a French
Certificate of Identity issued in Shanghai on July 5th,
1938.

Thanking you in anticipation,

I have the honour to be,
Sir,
Your obedient Servant,
[Signature]
Consul General for Italy.

To the Commissioner of Police
Shanghai Municipal Council
LOCAL

先生：

如蒙惠赐有关俄国侨民米娜·米赫利亚·韦利昌斯基（Mina Mikhlia Velickansky）夫人的尽可能详尽之资料，不胜感激。该夫人出生于1914年9月24日，出生地为赤塔（西伯利亚），持有1938年7月5日在上海签发的法国身份证明书。

先此致谢，

Sir,

I have the honour to acknowledge receipt

communicated to you in due course.

I have the honour to be,
Sir,

Commissioner of Police.
